claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside a package inherit the package's version.

Pulumi recommends the strategies described in this guide for structuring Git repositories used to publish packages, and following them improves reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed of packages.
Pulumi packages come in two flavors (source-based and executable-based), and each is versioned and released differently.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and the package's version is the Git tag on that repository.

Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow (apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`), typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
The publish step for source-based packages often runs automated tests before publishing.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Pulumi Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a `Pulumi.yaml` file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
The version of an executable-based package is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
In both source-based and executable-based cases, the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package.

The Pulumi IDP Private Registry documentation is located at /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/; packaging-components page has anchors #source-based-plugin-packages and #executable-based-plugin-packages; CLI reference exists at /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/.
Pulumi recommends that a repository contain exactly one Pulumi package, regardless of package type.
A repository containing multiple packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights the way Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
Multiple components inside a single Pulumi package are fine and expected, and the components ship together at the package's version.
Pulumi recommends defining exactly one package per repository, grouping a cohesive set of components in that package, and using multiple repositories (one per package) for distinct packages.
The importance of the one-package-per-repository principles grows as an organization's adoption of Pulumi grows.

The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry (https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/eks/) bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
The Amazon EKS package's components are almost always used together and tend to evolve together, so a shared semantic version makes sense.
One `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it in the repository.
The example repository layout places a single `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repo root with components under a `components/` directory (EksCluster/, EksIam/) as a valid layout for a Pulumi package.
Pulumi does not recommend using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components, because it forfeits meaningful semantic versioning.
When unrelated components share a package, every release of the package versions every component the same way regardless of whether each component changed, which violates semver.
In a package with two unrelated components, an enhancement to ComponentA yields v1.1.0 and a subsequent breaking change to ComponentB yields v2.0.0 for the whole package, per semver.
A semver Git tag such as `v1.2.3` is applied to the repository as part of publishing a source-based package.
The 'Publishing packages' page exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/ and covers publishing mechanics.
This guide covers versioning, cohesion, and monorepo trade-offs for structuring Git repositories when publishing Pulumi packages.
